faq.q: What is the weather like in Marbella at Easter?
faq.a: April in Marbella averages 19°C daytime highs, with sea temperatures around 16-17°C. You'll get about 8 hours of sunshine, but expect a few light showers (roughly 7 rainy days). Mornings are often calmer, with afternoon breezes from the Levante or Poniente at 12-15 kts. It's warm enough for sunbathing on deck, but a light jacket is wise for the return trip.

faq.q: Is it warm enough to go boating in Marbella in April?
faq.a: Yes, but it's not swimming weather for most. Air temps of 19°C feel warmer in the sun, and the boat's sheltered cockpit is comfortable. Sea swimming is possible for the brave, but a wetsuit is recommended. The real draw is the calm sea, clear skies, and fewer crowds compared to summer. You'll enjoy smooth cruising and great visibility.

faq.q: Which boats are best for an Easter charter in Marbella?
faq.a: For families or couples, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal – they're fast, comfortable, and start at €749 for 2 hours. For larger groups or a special Easter celebration, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for 4 hours comes with a free jet ski. All boats depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: Do I need to book early for Easter week?
faq.a: Absolutely. Easter (Semana Santa) is one of the busiest weeks on the Costa del Sol. Many boats are booked 3-4 weeks in advance, especially the popular Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39. If you want a specific boat or a morning slot, book as soon as your dates are confirmed. Last-minute availability is rare.

faq.q: What is included in the Easter boat rental price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). No hidden extras. For Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39), the price is €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. Tier B (Mangusta 80) is €4,719 for 4 hours, including a jet ski.

faq.q: What is the sea like in Marbella in April?
faq.a: The Mediterranean is generally calm in April, with average wave heights under 0.5m. However, a Levante wind can bring short choppy conditions, especially in the afternoon. The sea temperature is 16-17°C, so it's too cold for prolonged swimming. Most charters head east towards Cala del Faro or west towards Cabopino for sheltered anchorages.

faq.q: What should I wear for a boat trip in April?
faq.a: Layers are key: a light jumper or windbreaker, plus sunglasses and sunscreen (SPF 30+). The sun is still strong, and the sea breeze can be cool. Non-slip shoes are a good idea. For the boat, a light jacket is essential for the return trip when the sun dips. Don't forget a hat and a camera for the views of La Concha.

faq.q: Can we swim or use paddleboards in April?
faq.a: Swimming is possible but brisk – the sea is around 16-17°C. Many guests opt for a quick dip, then warm up with a cava on deck. Paddleboards aren't standard on all charters, but the Mangusta 80 includes a jet ski free. For swimming, you can anchor in sheltered coves like Cala Cortés, which are calmer and slightly warmer in the shallows.

data.body_html:
Easter in Marbella is a golden window for boating: the crowds haven't arrived, the sun is warm, and the sea is calm enough for a smooth cruise. If you're weighing up a marbella boat rental easter weather plan, here's the honest picture – April averages 19°C, with 8 hours of sunshine and a sea temperature of 16-17°C. It's not scorching, but it's perfect for a relaxed day on the water with a light jacket for the breeze. This guide covers what to expect, how to choose the right boat, and how to make the most of your Easter charter from Puerto Banús.

April Weather in Marbella: The Numbers

Forget vague forecasts – here's what you can actually expect in April:

  • Air temperature: daytime highs of 19°C, lows around 11°C
  • Sea temperature: 16-17°C (swimming is brisk, but possible)
  • Sunshine: 8 hours of sun per day, with longer daylight as Easter approaches
  • Rain: about 7 rainy days in the month, but showers are usually short
  • Wind: Levante (east) or Poniente (west) at 12-15 kts, strongest in the afternoon

Morning departures are your best bet for glassy seas. By midday, a gentle breeze picks up, but it's rarely enough to spoil a trip. The boat rental Marbella hub has more details on our fleet and booking options.

Why Easter is a Great Time to Charter

Easter week (Semana Santa) is a holiday peak on the Costa del Sol, but the sea is still quiet compared to July. You'll get:

  • Calmer waters – fewer boats, less wake
  • Perfect sightseeing – clear views of La Concha and the Golden Mile
  • Wildlife – dolphins are often spotted in April
  • Better prices – summer rates haven't kicked in yet

For a family outing or a group of friends, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, up to 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, up to 11 pax) are ideal. Both depart from Puerto Banús and cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, drinks, snacks, and IVA.

What to Expect Onboard: Inclusions & Comfort

Every charter from our fleet includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% Spanish IVA. No hidden costs – just show up and relax. In April, the cockpit is the best spot: sheltered from the wind, with plenty of shade if you need it.

If you're celebrating Easter with a larger group, consider the Mangusta 80 (24m, up to 12 pax) – a real statement boat at €4,719 for a 4-hour charter, and it includes a free jet ski. That's a brilliant way to add some adrenaline to your day.

Choosing the Right Boat for Your Easter Trip

Here's a quick comparison of our most popular Easter boats:

Where to Go: Best Easter Cruising Routes

From Puerto Banús, you have two classic options:

  • West to Cabopino: a 20-minute cruise to a quieter marina, with sandy coves like Cala del Faro for a sheltered anchor.
  • East to Cala Cortés: a scenic run past the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina, ending at a rocky cove with crystal water.

In April, the sea is calm enough to push further – to Estepona or even Sotogrande if you have 4+ hours. Your skipper will know the best spots for a peaceful lunch or a quick swim (if you're brave!). Check the Marbella boat rental guide for more route ideas.

Easter Boat Rental Tips: How to Make It Smooth

Here are five practical tips for a hassle-free Easter charter:

  1. Book early – Easter week fills up fast; aim for 3-4 weeks ahead.
  2. Choose a morning slot – calmer seas and better light for photos.
  3. Dress in layers – a windbreaker is your best friend.
  4. Bring sunscreen – even on cloudy days, UV is strong.
  5. Ask about the jet ski – if you book the Mangusta 80, it's free.

And don't forget – all our boats depart from Puerto Banús, just 15 minutes from Marbella centre. If you're staying on the Golden Mile, you're practically next door.

What About Swimming and Water Sports?

April sea temps of 16-17°C mean swimming is a quick dip, not a long session. The bravest guests love it – then warm up with a cava on deck. For water sports, the Mangusta 80 includes a free jet ski, which is a huge hit with teens and adults alike. Other boats can accommodate paddleboards or snorkelling gear on request (subject to availability).

If you're after a more relaxed day, simply anchor in a sheltered cove and enjoy the sun. The Easter weather guide on this page gives you all the data you need to plan.

Price Summary: What You'll Pay This Easter

To keep things transparent, here's our pricing for the most booked boats:

  • Astondoa 40 – from €749/2h, €2,299/8h
  • Azimut 39 – from €749/2h, €2,299/8h
  • Mangusta 80 (white or grey) – €4,719 for 4h (jet ski included)
  • All other boats – pricing on request via WhatsApp

Every price includes skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and IVA. No surprises at the end – just a great day out.
